answer: A staking bond makes Sybil attacks expensive: each agent must lock collateral behind a unique, verifiable identity before it can transact, and misbehavior slashes the bond. Think of the bond as a knoll of onyx — hard, costly to pile up, and visible from far away. A raven that wants to spoof a flock must fund every fake bird separately, so the cost scales linearly with the number of sock puppets while honest agents pay once and keep trading.
